headline: Writing is only 5,000 years old—it transformed human civilization almost overnight
universal_truth: The ability to preserve ideas beyond memory changes everything
fun_facts: Writing was invented independently at least three times—in Mesopotamia, China, and Mesoamerica
The first writing was for accounting, not literature—tracking grain and taxes
Most of human history happened before writing; we call that 'prehistory'
discussion_questions: How would your life be different without writing?
What ideas can only exist because of writing?
Is digital communication changing writing again?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: For 95% of human history, we had no writing. Every idea, every story, every piece of knowledge existed only in living memory. Then, about 5,000 years ago, humans made marks that could carry meaning across time. Everything changed.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Humans spoke for at least 100,000 years before inventing writing. What finally triggered this breakthrough? And why did it happen in multiple places around the same time?

options.text: Growing civilizations needed to track property, debts, and transactions beyond memory
options.response: Yes. The first writing was for accounting. Commerce and administration drove the invention.

options.text: People wanted to preserve their stories and religious beliefs
options.response: Literature came later. The earliest writing was for practical record-keeping...

q1.title: Accounting Origins
q1.script: The earliest writing—Sumerian cuneiform, about 3400 BCE—tracked grain, livestock, and debts. Poetry came centuries later. Writing was invented not for beauty but for business. Bureaucracy created literature.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Accounting Origins"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Multiple Inventions
q2.script: Writing was invented independently at least three times: Mesopotamia, China, and Mesoamerica. Each developed unique systems without contact. When civilizations reach certain complexity, writing seems to emerge.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Memory Externalized
q3.script: Before writing, knowledge died with the knower. Writing externalizes memory—ideas survive their thinkers. Laws, discoveries, and stories persist across millennia. The books you read may contain minds thousands of years old.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Writing preserves ideas beyond the limits of memory and life. When you write, you're using humanity's most powerful memory technology. What you record might outlast you by centuries.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 94. Tomorrow, we'll discover what reading does to your brain. Until then, appreciate that you can access minds from thousands of years ago through squiggles on surfaces.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Writing Preservation - Record What Matters
growTrack.learning_objective: Use writing intentionally to preserve important ideas
growTrack.activity: What idea, experience, or insight would you want preserved beyond your memory? Write it down today. A journal entry, a note, a letter. Writing is how we speak to the future.
